text:
Marathon Petroleum has gained 0.44% today, continuing a strong recovery after losing 6.76% over the past two weeks—the stock has climbed nearly $42 from its November 6th low. The uptick reflects two tailwinds for refiners: U.S. oil prices have risen to $89.62 per barrel (up from the lows that triggered the earlier sell-off), and heating oil prices are up 59% year-over-year as winter demand kicks in, which supports margins on the diesel and heating oil products refineries produce.

The broader picture is mixed but currently supportive. Refineries are running at 95.2% capacity—near maximum utilization—which means the industry is operating lean and any supply disruption or continued cold weather would tighten margins further. However, the recent news of Russian crude production rebounding and global oil markets shifting into surplus is a longer-term headwind that could eventually pressure both oil prices and refiner profits if it persists.
